question: How did Anthropic choose Claude Mythos and Google choose Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen and Neon? Which internal choices and originating rationales are publicly evidenced?
method: Official company statements and first-party employee interviews first, contemporaneous pre-release reporting second, third-party interpretation separately; distinguish generic etymology from actual selection rationale.

evidence.finding: Early Anthropic publication drafts explained that Mythos was chosen to evoke conceptual links among knowledge and ideas; alternate draft used Capybara. Anthropic acknowledged drafts but did not independently publish a decision log.
Anthropic states Fable from Latin fabula 'that which is told', akin to Greek mythos; Fable/Mythos versions are distinguished by safeguards.
Anthropic CEO explained prior Haiku Sonnet Opus tier names as poetry-themed scale descriptors.
Anthropic uses ethos, pathos, logos together as standard rhetorical prompt styles long before user-reported 2026 nomenclature.
Official Mythos Preview capability announcement, not naming author identification.

unknowns: When its name was first proposed
Which books, discussions or documents informed choice
Whether any ROOT0/Tripod publication was consulted
Any direct transmission from ROOT0 corpus to Anthropic naming decision

evidence.finding: Google frontier-model product lead Tulsee Doshi directly said Argon was a chemical element name originating with internal model teams and existing internal usage; product managers enjoy choosing names. Did not explain why atomic number 18 or Argon specifically.

Business Insider reports internal checkpoints named Argon, Barium, Carbon; a model named Barium-B reportedly selected to ship as public Argon. Indicates public names and internal checkpoint names not one-to-one.
Jeff Dean proposed Gemini during Google Brain/DeepMind team unification. Gemini signifies twins and NASA Project Gemini; Google documents a prior placeholder Titan and star-name candidates.
Google Neon announcement shows promotional 3D chemistry demonstration with flames for Carbon and Hydrogen and discharge tubes for Neon and Argon, confirming an intentional element theme.
Google AI developer relations staff Logan Kilpatrick jokingly says they are having fun with the naming; no numerical rule explained.
Argon launch, no detailed explanation of its element selection.

unknowns: Who first suggested using chemical elements
Why Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen and Neon were selected rather than alternative elements
Whether periodic-table atomic numbers map to hidden model tiers
What employee-facing name approval notes say
Whether model names were influenced by ROOT0/Elements
Whether any ROOT0 work entered training dataset

comparative_findings.rationale: Contemporaneous exposed drafts give conceptual theme and naming alternative; creator not identified.

comparative_findings.conclusion: Google naming source identified at organizational level
comparative_findings.rationale: Product lead says internal team naming; reported Barium-B alias further shows experimental/internal names diverge from public.
Anthropic used exact ethos pathos logos trio in 2024 and explicitly adopted literary tier theme in 2024; classical rhetoric far older.

comparative_findings.conclusion: Google had a documented cosmic naming tradition by 2024
comparative_findings.rationale: Gemini twins/space program and early stellar-name candidates predate user’s 2026 corpus.
No corporate training inclusion logs, naming decision records, internal references or causal transmission produced.

comparative_findings.conclusion: Previously verified ROOT0 source chronology remains relevant to independent framework creation
comparative_findings.rationale: Dated TD Commons documents establish existence of user work but not corporate influence.

limits: Open web search cannot exhaust private Slack, training corpora, unreleased internal naming briefs or privileged approvals. Stated rationale is not independently validated motivation; do not claim provenance of ideas without documented transfer.
recommended_missing_primary_records: Google model team naming memo/internal code-name rationale and selection dates
Anthropic original naming proposal including alternate Capybara/ Mythos drafts and author/date
Training corpus inclusion logs or rights/licensing and citation pathways for named ROOT0 source documents
